parsed.explanation: Federal entry, passport-marker, federal-facility and federal-custody rules create tier-1 traveler exposures, including discrepancy-based refusal/possible permanent ineligibility and documented severe immigration-custody abuse. The state adds operative public-accommodation, hate-crime, document and care protections and is placed in a low-risk group, with courts sometimes enjoining national orders. Those state remedies do not cancel federal screening, facilities or custody. No execution or imprisonment for being trans is documented, but outing can trigger exclusion, detention and severe custody harm.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition, X-marker passports stopped, existing X valid until expiry; cable directs refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; ACLU suit and court challenges continue; state issues X licences/IDs and corrected birth certificates, mainly resident-facing.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, investigation and possible lifetime ineligibility; state ID protections do not govern federal entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections model includes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State law in 2023 explicitly protects trans people in state correctional facilities, but July 2026 assessment finds shortfalls in incarcerated protections.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State custody protection does not documentedly override federal prison or immigration detention; detention after entry discrepancy is the severe pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; many states ban such use, with some criminal trespass provisions and a documented arrest elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State prohibits gender-identity discrimination in public accommodation; whether this state bans facility use is not reproduced in the inventory.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation protection may cover private/state venues, but does not cancel federal-facility bans or federal screening.

care_services.exposure: National measures restrict or propose restricting gender-affirming care, especially for minors, and some orders were later blocked or enjoined; exact operative scope is contested.
care_services.protection: State bars insurer discrimination and mandates coverage of medically necessary gender-affirming treatment from 2024, including public programme.
care_services.interaction: State coverage protects care sought in-state but does not override federal entry, custody, funding or minor-care enforcement exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: January 2025 order defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-identity policies, and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy uses 'radically pro-transgender' framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal and state hate-crime laws include gender identity; state added it to equal protection in 2022; courts have enjoined several national orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing interacts with discretionary border and law-enforcement decisions, while state constitutional and hate-crime protections provide partial local recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care, direct investigation/prosecution related to school social transition including names/pronouns, and ban trans athletes entering women's sports.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy on minors, has school anti-bullying protection, and mandates youth care coverage; care-shield bill was vetoed and 2025 school sports policy requires birth sex.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces federal/state school and care rules despite state coverage; a guardian may face investigation or funding consequences under national directives.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated state-level trans-violence incident or pattern is documented; airport guide warns screening can be invasive and outing; 2025 poll shows majority support birth-sex document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalties include gender identity, amended 2013, with a reporting hotline established January 2025.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Lack of documented incidents is not evidence of absence; police response at federal checkpoints is governed nationally, not by the state hotline.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and proposed health rules are unresolved; qualitative healthcare-equity and incarcerated-protection shortfalls have no figures, counts or dates.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several orders, litigation is active, legal-aid guidance exists, and state non-discrimination law is enforceable locally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies depend on which national measure is operative at travel and on the actor encountered; state remedies do not documentedly preempt federal action.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine, discretionary exclusion at entry with weak appeals, but this case has active litigation, some injunctions, state protections and no documented imprisonment for presentation, so it sits above 0.35.

Comparable for secondary screening, discretionary refusal and ward/document mismatch without execution, but documented federal custody sexual abuse and possible permanent ineligibility make this case more severe than 0.55.

Higher than 0.75 cases because brief detention there ends with release and compensation, whereas here discrepancy can cause refusal, lifetime ineligibility consideration, federal facility exclusion and severe custody harm.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is interaction-driven: state law protects a visitor in local housing, employment, public accommodation and insured care, and provides hate-crime recourse. But every visitor first passes federal entry under binary document rules; discrepancy can become refusal or fraud exposure, federal facilities follow birth sex, and any detention can enter federal custody with documented abuse and care removal. Minors face additional national school, sports and care directives. State protections therefore raise the score above the federal-only floor, while unresolved federal exposures and unquantified shortfalls keep it near the midpoint.
